fact: Antibiotics only kill bacteria, not viruses. They are ineffective against viral infections such as colds, flu, dengue, or viral bronchitis.
While turmeric (curcumin) has anti-inflammatory properties, it cannot cure diabetes. Diabetes requires proper medical management, diet control, and prescribed medication.

myth: papaya leaf juice cures dengue overnight
fact: Papaya leaf extract may support platelet count recovery, but it is not a cure for dengue virus. Dengue management relies on hydration, monitoring warning signs, and medical care.

myth: cold weather causes the common cold
fact: Colds are caused by viruses, not low temperature. Cold weather may cause people to stay indoors closer together, facilitating viral spread.

myth: drinking hot water kills coronavirus or influenza in the throat
fact: Drinking hot water stays in the digestive tract and does not destroy viruses in the respiratory tract or bloodstream.

myth: tuberculosis spreads through shaking hands or sharing food
fact: TB is spread through the air when a person with active lung TB coughs, sneezes, or speaks. It does not spread by touch, clothes, or sharing eating utensils.

myth: TB treatment can be stopped as soon as symptoms disappear
fact: Stopping TB treatment early can cause drug-resistant TB (MDR-TB). The full 6-month or longer course must be completed as prescribed by a doctor.

myth: pregnant women should eat for two
fact: Pregnant women need extra nutrients and slightly more calories (around 300 extra kcal/day in 2nd/3rd trimester), not double the amount of food.

myth: colostrum first milk should be thrown away
fact: Colostrum is rich in antibodies and protective nutrients. It is the baby's first immunization and should always be fed to the newborn immediately after birth.

myth: wearing a mask outdoors causes carbon dioxide poisoning
fact: Standard surgical and cloth masks allow oxygen and CO2 molecules to pass freely while filtering out larger droplets and respiratory particles.

myth: air purifiers eliminate all health risks of severe air pollution
fact: Air purifiers help indoor PM2.5 levels, but outdoor exposure, proper ventilation, and wearing N95 masks during severe AQI alerts remain critical.

myth: flood water is safe to drink if boiled for 5 seconds
fact: Flood water contains sewage, chemicals, and pathogens. Water must be brought to a rolling boil for at least 1 full minute or treated with chlorine tablets.

myth: mosquitoes carrying dengue only bite at night
fact: Aedes mosquitoes which transmit Dengue virus are primary day-biters, most active during early morning and late afternoon before dusk.
Extensive international scientific studies involving millions of children have repeatedly proven there is no link between vaccines and autism.
Garlic does not repel Aedes mosquitoes or prevent dengue virus transmission. Mosquito repellent and eliminating standing water are proven methods.

myth: herbal teas can replace insulin for type 1 diabetes
fact: Type 1 diabetes is an autoimmune condition requiring lifelong insulin replacement. Herbal remedies cannot replace insulin.
